result.reasoning:
The code reading is accurate but the finding is immaterial on this batch's inputs, and three of its load-bearing claims are factually wrong.

(1) DOCUMENTED, NOT SILENT. operator_weights()'s own docstring (steer.py:324-327) states the table holds "the weight of every rule whose pattern is led by that operator AT THE ROOT OR ANYWHERE. Structure-specific rules lose their context here (that is what `accept` is for); this is the fallback, not the mechanism." The root-aware mechanism (Guidance.banned / accept, idea_search.py:225,231) is correct; OPW is the declared coarse prior.

(2) ONLY 5 OF THE 9 ZERO ENTRIES ARE REAL. cs_max, cs_min and ts_zscore are NOT in AlphaCube's registry at all (default_registry().list_all()), so OPW.get(s.name, 1.0) is never consulted for them -- dead keys. ts_product=0.0 is CORRECT: B5 is not root-anchored. The root-anchor loss removes exactly 5 operators: cs_mean, cs_sum, cs_median, cs_stddev_full, cross_zscore. D2/D3/D13 emit multipliers (0.3/0.5/0.6), not removals.

(3) ONE CONSUMER, AND IT PRODUCED NOTHING TO DISTORT. grep over the repo: the only production caller of operator_weights() is scripts/idea_search.py:182. No sweep, selection, holdout read, Sharpe or annualised-excess number touches it. The only episode that ran both arms, episodes/e1_I2_dispersion_fold/evidence.json, reports steer 123 scored / 102 live / 0 passers and control 170 scored / 130 live / 0 passers. independent_distinct and efficiency_per_100 were never computed (the allp block is skipped when nothing clears THR), there is no episode.md, and no steer-vs-control efficiency number appears anywhere in docs/ or handoff/. So the "E6 steer-vs-control episode numbers" the finding says are corrupted do not exist: both arms are 0.

(4) THE CONTROL ARM, WITH ALL 5 OPS AVAILABLE AND UNIFORM SAMPLING, USED NONE OF THEM. Operator histograms over both arms' archived candidates in evidence.json: cs_mean, cs_sum, cs_median, cs_stddev_full, cross_zscore, ts_product, cs_rank, cross_stddev, ts_stddev, cross_min, ts_min all appear 0 times -- in the steer arm AND in the control arm. The restriction cost the steer arm nothing observable. Consistent with the steer arm's banned counter being 0 across 430 proposals; its dominant filter was outside=243/430 (the MUST neighbourhood), then thinned=20.

(5) QUANTIFIED SAMPLING SHIFT IS 1-3%. Computed exactly over AlphaCube's real _producers lists under the steer `pick`, current OPW vs the finding's proposed fix: P(drawing one of the 5 genuinely-dropped ops) = 0.0165 (daily), 0.0171 (collapsed, root), 0.0028 (full); total variation = 0.025 / 0.025 / 0.006; P(drawing an idea operator) moves 0.4372 -> 0.4270. The "one-sided penalty list" claim also ignores BOOST=8 at idea_search.py:199, which multiplies ~12 idea operators and dominates every OPW entry -- the steer arm's up-weight comes from BOOST, not from the U-rules.

(6) THE 12 "UNREACHABLE GOOD CANDIDATES" ARE UNREACHABLE EITHER WAY. Reproduced from tmp/review/matcher-guidance/rows.json: 414 rows at ul_sharpe>=2.0, 12 with a non-root cs_*/cross_zscore. Of those 12, FIVE are hard-banned by the correct root-aware G.banned() path (B3 day-scalar multiplier, B4 epsilon denominator) -- including 3 of the 5 the finding headlines: h_gate_vol_mix (2.58), h_gate_lowvol (2.26), h_rv_fold_state_weight (2.25). Fixing operator_weights() would not make them reachable. The other 7 pass accept() only at probability 0.0225 (h_ov_state), 0.075 (h_gate_disp_mix), 0.25-0.75 (F115 family). All 12 have depth 5-13 and 13-128 nodes against the GP's min_depth=2 / max_depth=4 (idea_search.py:262) on a 192-evaluation budget; the control arm's archive tops out at depth 6. 11 of 12 also fail the I1 MUST filter.

(7) NO BOOST CONFLICT IN THIS BATCH. None of B01.yaml's 5 ideas names any of the 5 removed operators in its grammar or seeds, so BOOST*0=0 never bites.

Impact is nil, not merely inside the +-0.3 Sharpe / +-3pt band: there is no number to move.

result.corrected_fix:
No change is needed for any reported number. Two notes if the parent wants to harden it anyway:

DO NOT apply the suggested change to operator_weights() (skip any rule with r.pattern.root). It changes the steer arm's sampling distribution, so it must not land between a steer run and the control run it is compared against -- episodes/e1_I2_dispersion_fold would have to be re-run for the two arms to stay comparable. It also discards information the docstring deliberately keeps: a root ban is still evidence the operator is weak, and the coarse table is explicitly the place where context is dropped.

If a guard is wanted, the minimal one is a FLOOR on root-anchored rules inside operator_weights(), not a skip -- emit max(r.w, 0.1) (or 0.1 in place of 0.0 for a root ban) when r.pattern.root is set. That keeps the directional prior, guarantees a root-only ban can never delete an operator from the grammar, and makes the second half of the suggestion (an epsilon floor in idea_search) unnecessary, so the sampling hook keeps its single meaning of "w <= 0 means this operator is globally banned".

The one latent hazard worth a line in the handoff, which the finding does not state: BOOST * 0.0 == 0.0 at scripts/idea_search.py:199, so a FUTURE idea whose grammar or seeds names cs_mean / cs_sum / cs_median / cs_stddev_full / cross_zscore would lose that operator from its own neighbourhood despite the 8x boost, and the run would look like a normal search. Verified that none of B01.yaml's five ideas (I1..I5) names any of them, so nothing run so far is affected. The floor above fixes this too; alternatively skip OPW for operators in IDEA_OPS.
